"What's she like?" they whisper.|Another summoned first-year on the bench, another whisper: "Is it true she can read minds?"|The waiting bench has a first-year on it again; you suspect it always will. "Have you been in? What happens?"} {The stone owl watches you both.|Somewhere above, a door opens and closes.|{final_year: You remember sitting there yourself, a hundred years ago, last week.|The summons is smudged from being held so hard.}} Tell them the kind truth {"She'll listen," you say, "and it will be worse than shouting, and then it will be better." The first-year breathes for the first time in an hour.|"She can't read minds," you say. "She just doesn't need to." The first-year laughs, shakily, and goes up a little taller.|"She'll pour you tea," you say. "Drink it. Tell her the truth." The first-year nods and goes up the stair like someone visiting a friend.} Tell them a horror story {You describe the trapdoor, the pit and the crocodiles in loving detail. The first-year goes up grey. You feel wonderful, then less wonderful.|"Only on Thursdays," you say gravely. It's Thursday. The first-year's face is a work of art.|You tell them about the owl that eats liars. The owl, above you, opens one eye and looks at you for a long time.}
